moat_against: Gross margin compressed 95.7% (2021) → 46.2% (2025) as product-sales mix grew — no consolidated pricing-power evidence
Concentration in two aging engine platforms (CFM56, V2500) whose fleets shrink from here
OEM (CFM/GE/Safran) and Willis Lease competition for the same aftermarket
No computable filed ROIC history (operating income untagged); ~10x debt/equity leverage
moat_for: Leading independent CFM56/V2500 aftermarket scale — largest narrowbody engine fleets with a long run-out tail
MRE module-exchange model: airlines buy green time instead of full shop visits — real cost/time advantage
SCI vehicles create captive MRE demand — SPV engines serviced exclusively by FTAI shops
moat_justification: Leading independent CFM56/V2500 aftermarket position with a genuine module-exchange (MRE) cost/time advantage, PMA parts, and captive SCI demand; but gross margin fell 95.7% (2021) to 46.2% (2025) as product sales mix grew, roic_proxy is not computable from filed tags (no ROIC history above cost of capital to cite), the franchise is concentrated in two aging engine platforms, and the balance sheet carries ~10x debt/equity. CAP = 8.5 years.
name: FTAI AVIATION LTD.
one_liner: Real CFM56/V2500 aftermarket franchise (moat 5/10) priced like a compounder at $169.29, but conservative owner's earnings are negative on every filed basis — median -$2.00/sh, FY2025 -$3.47/sh, TTM -$4.86/sh — so no OE DCF supports the price and it cannot clear the 15% hurdle; Tier F.
